The language has 18 consonants /p, t, c, k, β, l, j, ɣ, m, n, ɲ, ŋ, mb, nd, ɲɟ, ŋg, w, h/ and 7 vowels /i, ɪ, ɛ, a, ɔ, ʊ, u/. It has a predictable tone melody of Low-High-Low (LHL) with verbs showing L tones for prefixes, H for the stem, and L for the final syllable. new_statements.rule_in_words: The native-speaker author describes Ndendeule prosody in tonal terms only: verbs carry a predictable (non-lexical) L-H-L melody — prefixes low, stem high, word-final syllable low (2017: melody assigned from the right edge, i.e. final L preceded by H); a word-final H occurs only as the imperfective marker -á or from truncation. He states explicitly that the tone system is otherwise undescribed and says nothing about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: Final-syllable H tone marks imperfective aspect (-á) or results from truncation (Ngonyani 2017:177); nouns' tonal behaviour not described.
new_statements.domain_note: Statement concerns verbs (word-level melody); no statement for nouns, citation forms or phrase-level prominence. The predictable LHL melody with final L is consistent with a reduced/predictable tone system of the southern-Tanzanian type but the source does not call it stress or locate a single prominent syllable.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe the Mkongo (Namtumbo District, Ruvuma Region) variety, the author's native dialect; language = Glottolog nden1249 (names Ndendeule/Ndendeuli/Kindendeule/Kindendeβuli), Guthrie-Maho N101. Not to be confused with nden1248 (Ndengereko/Ndengeleko, P11).
